solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, directions as headed); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: British settle historical Irish problem

parts.note: to light on something is to come to rest on it, as a bird settles

explanation.surface: Britain is told to sort out an old Irish trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to the potato blight behind the Irish Famine of the 1840s.
explanation.definitionFit: The potato disease that caused the Great Famine in Ireland is the classic historical example of crop disease.

clue.text: Shoot a troublesome person in European city

parts.note: a bud is a young shoot on a plant
taken as written
a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: A violent instruction to gun down a nuisance in a foreign capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Shoot looks like a verb of violence; it is a plant shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital of Hungary, an example of a city in Europe.

clue.text: Have reason for negative conclusion and fire, with disastrous consequences

parts.note: to infer is to reason one's way to a judgement
no is a refusal, a negative verdict

explanation.surface: Someone reasons out a gloomy outcome to a disastrous blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a huge, destructive blaze.

clue.text: Person following rigid policy in firm over cosmetic

indicators.note: in a down answer the first part sits above the second

parts.note: hard means firm, not soft
liner is make-up for outlining eyes or lips

explanation.surface: An uncompromising boss in a cosmetics company.
explanation.walkthrough: Firm looks like a company; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardliner sticks to an uncompromising position, refusing to bend.

clue.text: Former partner, told of blame, losing head throughout

indicators.note: each of the three words drops its first letter, so heads are lost all the way through the phrase

explanation.surface: An ex, informed that they are at fault, keeps losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Behead told, of and blame in turn and the pieces run together.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is an idiom for someone you once had a romance with.

clue.text: People from south of US caught, trapped by weird Martian aliens

indicators.note: the letter for caught is held inside the reshuffled letters
something weird is strange, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Strange beings from Mars have captured someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Mexico, Central and South America, all lying south of the United States.

clue.text: Following defeat, try to get the bit between your teeth?

definitions.text: try to get the bit between your teeth?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a defeat is a loss in a game or contest

explanation.surface: After losing, someone resolves to get to grips with things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get the bit between your teeth' is an idiom for getting determined; read literally it is clearing a stuck bit of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental thread is drawn between teeth to remove trapped food.

clue.text: Not the winner in final, so ranted

indicators.note: the answer sits within the run of letters in the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of final, the word so and the start of ranted

explanation.surface: A loser in the final had a rant about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a competitor who finishes without a place, an unsuccessful entrant.

clue.text: Without difficulty, see while one is inside

indicators.note: the pieces sit within the name of the see

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and diocese in Cambridgeshire, a bishop's see
as can mean while, at the same time

explanation.surface: Easy to see while someone is indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: See is a bishop's diocese here, not to look.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something easily means managing it with no effort or trouble.

clue.text: They support lines in paper followed by some Europeans

indicators.note: the paper's name comes first, then the nationality

parts.note: The Telegraph is a British newspaper, as is this very puzzle's home
Poles are people from Poland

explanation.surface: Writing in a newspaper about who backs certain lines, followed by a group of Europeans.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden posts carrying overhead telephone and telegraph wires.

clue.text: Delay of French Revolution's effect

parts.note: de is the French word for of
ferment is the agitation and unrest a revolution stirs up

explanation.surface: A question of how the French Revolution was put off.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R suggests the French Revolution of 1789, but the words split into a French word and a word for turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: A deferment is a postponement, as of payment or of military call-up.

clue.text: Nothing, in its current state, provides refuge

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
as is means unchanged, just as it stands

explanation.surface: Doing nothing and leaving things as they are offers a kind of shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert spring is a place of shelter, and figuratively any haven of calm.

clue.text: Offender who's out taking a part in educational exercise

indicators.note: the word for school exercise takes in the other pieces, holding them between its two letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise at school
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A released prisoner joins in a school activity.
explanation.definitionFit: A parolee is a prisoner let out early on conditions of good behaviour.

clue.text: Zero silt spread around river — that allows flow under bridge

parts.note: no means none at all, zero

indicators.note: the scrambled silt goes around the letter for river
the letters of silt are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mud has spread around a river with nothing left flowing under the bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge is the bridge of the nose, not one over the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Each opening of the nose sits beneath its bony ridge and lets air pass in and out.

clue.text: Promised almost complete choice of quarters

indicators.note: the word for choice sits among the remaining compass points
the full set of compass points is cut short, one of the four left out

parts.note: the four quarters of the compass are its cardinal points
or introduces an alternative, a choice

explanation.surface: Someone pledged a nearly full selection of rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarters are the compass points; read the answer as 'S, W or N'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sworn is to have made a solemn oath or promise.

clue.text: Dismissal is touching and poignant

parts.note: re means concerning, touching on
moving means stirring the emotions

explanation.surface: Being sacked is an emotional, poignant affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Touching looks like a synonym for poignant, but it is the word meaning about.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing someone from office is dismissing them, the act of ousting.

clue.text: Very bad service area? Just the opposite

definitions.text: Very bad service area? Just the opposite

parts.words: Very bad service area? Just the opposite
parts.note: reads like a grumble about a motorway stop, but vice is wickedness and the Latin tag means the other way round

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a dreadful motorway service area; the answer is the Latin tag for the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used to say that the converse also holds, the reverse case.

clue.text: Kind of Chinese soldier, for the most part audacious

parts.note: a man is a private soldier

indicators.note: the word for audacious loses its final letter, keeping most of it

parts.note: daring means bold

explanation.surface: A Chinese soldier who is mostly brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandarin is the main spoken form of Chinese, a variety of the language.

clue.text: The writer's supporting theatre that's turned vulgar

parts.note: the setter speaking: I am, shortened
pro means in favour of

indicators.note: the word for the theatre is turned round

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A writer backs a theatre that has gone crude.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper describes something indecent or coarse, in bad taste.

clue.text: Name of woman I got into male golf club

indicators.note: the I goes inside the letters for male and golf club

parts.note: the R and A is the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman sneaks into a men-only golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf club is the R and A, the Royal and Ancient at St Andrews in Scotland, not an iron or wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Miranda is a girl's given name, the heroine of The Tempest.

clue.text: Line dancing with sidekicks?

parts.note: sidekicks reads as companions, but the dancers in single file kick out to the side

explanation.walkthrough: Sidekicks look like friends tagging along; here they are literal kicks to the side.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin-American party dance where people hold the person in front and kick sideways on the beat.

clue.text: Time's up for least sophisticated locals

indicators.note: time's up here means the letter for time climbs higher in the down answer, from last place to third

parts.note: naivest means most innocent and unworldly
the tail of the word for least sophisticated, with the time letter at its end
the same letters with the time letter now at the top of the run

explanation.surface: Time is up for the simplest people in the area.
explanation.walkthrough: Time's up looks like a deadline; it tells you to move the T upwards in the word for least sophisticated.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives are people born in a place, its local inhabitants.

clue.text: Standard academic is what?

parts.note: par is the normal level, as in golf
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a typical lecturer is.
explanation.definitionFit: Pardon? is a polite request to repeat something unheard.

clue.text: He, symbolically, is what gets it off the ground

definitions.text: He, symbolically, is what gets it off the ground

parts.words: He, symbolically, is what gets it off the ground
parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium, not a pronoun, and that gas gives lift to a craft lighter than air

explanation.walkthrough: He looks like a man; it is the element symbol for helium, which lifts a dirigible.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirigible balloon is a lighter-than-air craft kept aloft by helium.

clue.text: Quickly move married quarters for women

parts.note: to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: A newly married couple dash to change living quarters for the women.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women's section of a Muslim household.

clue.text: Really wanted commander checked, but it's half-hearted

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer

indicators.note: the doubled middle letter of the word for checked is halved to one

parts.note: vetted means examined carefully

explanation.surface: A commander longed for something but carried out the checks without enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet something is to desire it strongly, often what belongs to another.

clue.text: Benefactor has name inscribed in entrance

indicators.note: the letter for name is written into the word for entrance

parts.note: a door is the way in to a building

explanation.surface: A patron has their name carved over the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money or goods to a cause, as a benefactor does.

clue.text: Come down right on top of vehicle

parts.note: land means to come down to earth
over means above

explanation.surface: Something drops down and lands right on a car's roof.
explanation.walkthrough: A Land Rover is a British make of four-wheel-drive off-road vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand name is a well-known British off-road car, an example of a vehicle.

clue.text: Approach young woman, creating scary incident

parts.note: to near is to draw close
miss is the title of an unmarried girl

explanation.surface: Going up to a girl leads to a frightening moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is a narrow escape from collision or disaster.

clue.text: Doctor involved in many cases erasing hospital from schedule?

indicators.note: the hospital letter is wiped out of the phrase for schedule

parts.note: what's on is a listing of events

explanation.surface: A busy doctor drops the hospital from a timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The cases are detective cases, not medical ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Watson is Sherlock Holmes's companion and narrator of the detective stories.
